problem: Which of the following is the graph of  $y=-{(\frac{3}{10})}^{x+1}?$
worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y={(\frac{3}{10})}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/a9b6c2b12c1bc4bc7794dd5d409a99c61bf256ea58f9a016657cbbea5ef6b1e4.png)

 

- Horizontally shift it by $1$ units to the left to give $y={(\frac{3}{10})}^{x+1}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(-1,1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/5f4c0e3c4573f6e3167390d54ee21bbb8bf6e3879fcc06e7adf9d311e80ccb62.png)

- Then, reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-{(\frac{3}{10})}^{x+1}.$ The point $(-1,1)$ moves to $(-1,-1)$ and the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/b541282b8661f2fb28d0ce1f10c22a9a8cc7b083460c05093a89722bc084d7b9.png)
